title: Emergent capacity hedge playbook for mid-cycle spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: mid-cycle usage spikes and customer onboarding surges are causing ad-hoc scope cuts and emergency all-hands that disrupt planned work. We lack a lightweight, repeatable playbook to redistribute capacity, protect critical launches, and communicate scope trade-offs to stakeholders.

Goal: create an operational playbook and decision tree that PMs and Eng leads can execute within 24 hours to hedge capacity for 1-3 week surges without derailing the remainder of the cycle. Playbook should cover detection thresholds, tranche reallocation steps, communication templates, and a minimal set of approvals required.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page playbook exists in Confluence with step-by-step tranche reallocation actions
Engineering and Design leads sign off on emergency cut criteria and guaranteed minimal staffing for ongoing SLAs
Two sample runbooks are documented: (a) <10% surge reuse plan, (b) >30% sustained surge plan
Communication templates for customers, execs, and internal teams are ready and reviewed
A post-mortem template and telemetry dashboard widget are created to measure impact within the next cycle
outcome_metrics: Time-to-decision for surge response reduced to < 6 hours
Percentage of cycles requiring unscheduled all-hands reduced by 60%
Net scope slippage across non-urgent work limited to < 3 story-points per team on average
Customer-facing incident count due to capacity constraints reduced by 50%
risks: Overuse of hedge may create churn for low-priority work and morale issues
Ambiguous ownership could cause delays; need explicit approvers and fallback contacts
Metric noise: false-positive surge detection could trigger unnecessary reorganizations
next_steps: Draft initial one-page playbook and decision tree (owner: PM)
Run tabletop exercise with 3 Eng teams and Design to validate cut criteria (owner: Eng Lead)
Create telemetry dashboard card for surge detection and projected capacity impact (owner: Observability)
Publish playbook in Confluence and schedule 30-min training for PM/Eng leads
